body:
`frontend/src/pages/Catalog.tsx:105-106` offers `Compact` and `Dense` as adjacent
options in one density select. In `nl` BOTH msgids are translated "Compact", so the
dropdown shows the same label twice and one option is unreachable by name.

Found by auditing SPA-anchored msgids for the tell CWNG READER named: **one
translation serving two different msgids**. That check needs no knowledge of the
language, which is what makes it usable — the same session found `Black` translated
as "Back" in eight locales and `One column` as "Invalid read column".

Pre-existing on main; not introduced by the multi-device annotation work, which only
surfaced it by anchoring the msgids. The fix is a reviewed Dutch string for one of the
two (e.g. "Compact" / "Dicht"), NOT clearing a fuzzy flag — no flag is set here, so
the gate is silent and correct while the output is wrong.

The general trap: reusing a classic msgid looks like free translation coverage, and
the fuzzy gate only catches entries someone marked. A confidently-wrong translation
that nobody flagged passes every gate.
title: Dutch renders the Compact and Dense density options identically
